rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Hardy-Weinberg: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (p = dominant allele freq, q = recessive)
Natural selection: variation → struggle → survival of fittest → adaptation
Evolution (modern): change in allele frequencies in a population over generations

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Natural selection vs genetic drift:** selection is non-random, direction-giving; drift is random change in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations.  ·  **Darwinism vs neo-Darwinism:** Darwin lacked the inheritance mechanism; the modern synthesis adds Mendelian genetics, mutation, drift and isolation.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear Lamarck vs Darwin comparison.  ·  The modern synthesis (Neo-Darwinism) is the "correct" current theory; know its components.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Biston betularia*** — peppered moth; the textbook live demonstration of selection.  ·  ***Weismann's mice*** — 22 generations of tail-cutting, all born tailed: acquired characters not inherited.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Selection needs three ingredients:** variation, heritability, differential success — remove any one and evolution stalls. Selection does not create variation; it filters it.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Lamarckism: vital forces, new needs, use/disuse, inheritance of acquired characters; giraffe by stretching; disproved by Weismann's germplasm theory (tail-cutting mice).  ·  Darwinism: overproduction → struggle → variation → survival of the fittest → selection and inheritance → descent with modification; example: industrial melanism (Biston betularia), giraffe, antibiotic resistance.  ·  Neo-Darwinism: mutation + recombination + gene flow + selection + drift + isolation → allele-frequency change → speciation.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Darwin and Wallace presented their idea jointly in 1858 — one of science's rare independent double discoveries.

rows.label: MCQ drill
